scenes.text: Imagine walking up to a lake and seeing perfectly preserved, bone-dry statues of birds and bats frozen in mid-air poses.
The water here is so hostile, its pH levels can reach a burning twelve, which is almost as caustic as ammonia.
If a creature dips into this water, its body gets calcified, coated in sodium carbonate, and essentially turned to stone.
Yet, amazingly, a species of flamingos actually uses this deadly lake as their safest breeding ground because predators can't reach them.
